definitions: A cognitive bias where better-informed individuals find it difficult to think about problems from the perspective of lesser-informed individuals.
The difficulty experienced by an expert in explaining their knowledge to a novice, because the expert assumes a certain level of background knowledge.
examples: The professor suffered from the curse of knowledge when trying to teach the basics.
It's hard to explain complex code without falling victim to the curse of knowledge.
The marketing team needed to overcome the curse of knowledge to connect with new customers.
